newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX drops in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX drops in quiet trade.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in quiet trade on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with losses to several heavily-weighted issues driving the 16-share SAX index down 1.73 points to 204.65.
Oil refiner Slovnaft closed down only five crowns at 995, but its average price -- used for calculating the index -- eased 2.9 percent to help lead the bourse lower.

"There is not enough Slovnaft shares available on the market at the moment, and though demand continues, it is not strong enough to push the issue back through its nominal (1,000 crown) value," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Steel maker VSZ rose five crowns to close at 700, but its average price also dropped, by 0.3 percent, adding to SAX's fall.
Brokers said they expected lower demand seen for VSZ stock over the past few days to push it even lower, but added that this was the share's typical cyclical movements.
Commercial bank VUB dropped one crown, to close at 1,700, but brokers noted that the share traded only insignificant volume of seven shares. Oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade at all.
Overall volume rose to 389,434 shares, boosted by direct tardes, from 374,909 stocks traded on Thursday. Turnover increased to 254.84 million crowns, from 211.58 million on Thursday.
